_readme: Card examples for the rarity guide. Every entry points at a real card so the
page shows the actual printed symbol rather than a drawing of one.
`zoom` is the bottom corner crop, as a CSS background-position. Modern cards
carry the symbol bottom-LEFT; XY era and older carry it bottom-RIGHT.
SLANG ENTRIES CARRY THEIR OWN EXAMPLE. `show` is 'card' for a whole card,
'crop' for the magnified bottom-left corner, and the key is absent when no
honest picture exists. Cards here are deliberately DIFFERENT from the ladder
above: the reader gets a second worked example of each term, not a repeat.
NEVER TYPE A PRICE INTO AN `example`. Name the card instead, with
`priceOf: {set, number}`, and build-rarity.mjs reads the figure out of
public/data/cards/<set>.json and formats it with the same moneyCompact
every other page uses. The Hit entry used to read '. $1,470' as literal
text while the checklist said $1,470.58 and /complete-a-set.html said
$1,471, so the site quoted two different prices for one card and the
typed one could never catch up. Works on any entry in any list here.
THREE TERMS HAVE NO IMAGE, and that is not an oversight:
RH. TCGdex serves one scan per card, of the NORMAL printing. It has no
reverse-holo scan: variants_detailed lists a reverse variant but its image
field is null. Showing the normal card labeled 'reverse holo' would teach
the opposite of the thing the entry exists to teach.
fake-cards page.
WHAT NOT TO PUT ON THIS PAGE, all checked and deliberately left off:
Shiny Rare's symbol being a HOLLOW gold star. Bulbapedia says hollow,
Pokemon's own site says 'sparkling', and the scans were not sharp enough
to settle it. The whole claim is the hollow-vs-solid distinction, so it is
not worth publishing half-right.
Mega Attack Rare's pastel star symbol. Single-sourced, unverified.
Futuristic Rare. Real, but it does not exist in anyone's hands until the
30th Celebration lands on 16 September 2026.
A card for Rainbow rares. The whole claim is the rainbow FOIL, and a flat
scan does not show foil, so the picture would prove nothing the words do
not already say. The other eight retired mechanics are things you can SEE
in a scan, which is why they have one.
`offLadder` IS FOR RARITIES THIS SITE'S OWN CHECKLISTS PRINT THAT THE
LADDER ABOVE DOES NOT COVER. The failure case it exists for: somebody pulls
a card, reads the name off a set page here, looks it up on this page and
finds nothing. Counted across public/data/cards on 15 August 2026, Holo Rare
covers 88 cards and Black White Rare 4, and neither string appeared anywhere
on this page. Entries render with the magnified corner, same as the ladder,
because the symbol is the whole claim in both cases.
NOT EVERY UNCOVERED NAME BELONGS HERE. Checked on the same pass and left
where they already were: Holo Rare V, VMAX and VSTAR are the `gone` entry
'V, VMAX and VSTAR'; Radiant Rare is the `gone` entry 'Radiant Pokemon';
Secret Rare is the glossary term, the number shortcut and an FAQ answer.
Those are covered in prose under the name printed on the card rather than
the name a checklist API returns, which is the right way round.
EVERY ENTRY HERE CARRIES ITS `sources`, with the url and the date it was
read. Official Pokemon sources first, then Bulbapedia. Where a claim is
about the printed symbol it is also checked against the card scan the entry
shows, so a reader holding the card can settle it without either of us.
SLAB IS A DIAGRAM, NOT A PHOTO, and that is deliberate. We own no graded
cards, and a grading company's product photography is theirs. A labeled
schematic teaches the thing a photo would: where the grade sits, where the
cert number is, that the card is sealed and cannot be removed without
destroying the holder. It is captioned as a schematic so nobody mistakes it
for a real slab. Same approach as the fake-cards diagram.
Grading still has no image: it is a process, not an object.

ladder.name: Common
ladder.look: Plain card, matte finish, artwork sitting in a window. The bulk of every pack.

ladder.name: Uncommon
ladder.look: Looks the same as a Common to the naked eye. Most Trainer cards land here.

ladder.name: Rare
ladder.look: In modern sets these are always holo: foil on the artwork window, matte everywhere else.

ladder.name: Double Rare
ladder.look: A Pokemon ex in an ordinary card frame. The everyday ex, and the only high tier that still looks like a normal card.

ladder.name: Ultra Rare
ladder.look: Full art. The character fills the whole card, no artwork window, usually textured.

ladder.name: Illustration Rare
ladder.look: Full art of a normal Pokemon, not an ex, painted into a scene. The "Pokemon in its habitat" look.

ladder.name: Special Illustration Rare
ladder.look: Full art of an ex or a Supporter in a scene, with glitter over it. Usually the most valuable card in a set.

ladder.name: ACE SPEC Rare
ladder.look: A magenta and cyan Trainer or Special Energy. You are only allowed one in a deck, which is the whole point of them.

ladder.name: Hyper Rare
ladder.look: The whole card is gold, borders and all. Unmistakable across a room.

ladder.name: Mega Hyper Rare
ladder.look: Gold etched Mega Evolution ex with artwork drawn for it rather than a gold recolor of an existing card.
ladder.note: New to the Mega Evolution era. The symbol is a single four pointed sparkle with a heavy black outline, not three stars: several guides get this wrong.

offLadder.name: Black White Rare
offLadder.era: Black Bolt and White Flare, July 2025
offLadder.symbol: Two stars, the first filled in and the second an outline
offLadder.body: A full art printed in one colour the whole way through. The artwork, the border, the text and the symbol are all black or all white, with no gold anywhere, so it does not read as a top tier card even though it is numbered past the set total. Victini is the odd one out and prints red instead.
offLadder.ladder: Two stars again, so counting alone will not place it. The tell is that the second star is hollow rather than filled, and that neither star is silver or gold. It is its own thing rather than a rung above Special Illustration Rare, and only these two sets have it: Victini and Zekrom ex in Black Bolt, Victini and Reshiram ex in White Flare.
offLadder.example: Zekrom ex, Black Bolt. The corner reads 172/086

sources.for: The Pokemon Company press release, dated 6 May 2025. Names the rarity and says the cards 'will feature card illustrations in a monochromatic black or white design'. Also the 18 July 2025 release date for both sets.

'The rarity symbol for these cards are two stars, one black and one white.' Also that it has only been printed in these two sets, that the three Pokemon are Victini, Zekrom ex and Reshiram ex, and that the Victini card is red rather than monochrome.

The printed corner, which is what the figure shows. Checked on all three: sv10.5b/171 Victini, sv10.5b/172 Zekrom ex and sv10.5w/173 Reshiram ex each print one solid star followed by one hollow star, bottom left. THE COLOUR IS NOT CLAIMED HERE. Bulbapedia says black and white; on a flat scan of a foil symbol both stars read grey, so this page claims only the fill, which the scan does settle.

offLadder.name: Holo Rare
offLadder.era: Sword and Shield sets and older
offLadder.symbol: One black star, the same symbol a plain Rare carries
offLadder.body: Not a symbol of its own and not a rung of its own. A Holo Rare is a Rare with foil on the artwork window, and the corner prints the same single black star either way. Crown Zenith has both: Entei at 021/159 is the Holo Rare, Bellossom at 003/159 is the plain one, and the two corners are identical.
offLadder.ladder: It sits exactly where Rare sits on the ladder above. Older checklists split the two and list them as separate lines, which is where the name comes from, so you will meet it on the Sword and Shield set guides here and not on a Scarlet and Violet one. Some checklists print the same tier the other way round, as Rare Holo.
offLadder.example: Entei, Crown Zenith. The corner reads 021/159

sources.for: The Rare section lists the sub-classifications: 'Regular Rare, which are marked with [one star] but do not have any holofoil design' and 'Holofoil Rare, which are marked with [one star] and also have a Holofoil design on the card art'. Same symbol, different finish.

The printed corner. Compared bottom left crops of swsh12.5/021 Entei (Holo Rare) against swsh12.5/003 Bellossom (Rare), and swsh10.5/010 Charizard and swsh6/28 Cinderace (both Holo Rare) against swsh6/10 Abomasnow (Rare). All five print one black star.

Which sets on this site use the name. Holo Rare appears in celebrations, chilling-reign, crown-zenith, pokemon-go, rebel-clash and shining-fates, and in no Scarlet and Violet or Mega Evolution set. The Rare Holo word order comes from the other price feed and is what the older set guides here print.

slang.meaning: Illustration Rare. One gold star, full art of a non-ex Pokemon in a scene.
Special Illustration Rare. Two gold stars. Usually the best card in the set.
Alternate art. Collector slang, not a printed rarity. On a modern card it almost always means an IR or an SIR.
slang.example: Groudon, Paradox Rift. An Illustration Rare

slang.meaning: Full art. The illustration covers the whole card with no artwork window.
Reverse holo. Foil on everything except the artwork. Does not change the card's rarity.
Ultra Rare. Two silver stars, a full art ex.
Any card out of a pack worth meaningfully more than the pack cost.
The one card everybody is opening the set hoping to find.
slang.example: Mega Charizard X ex, the Phantasmal Flames chase

slang.meaning: Commons, uncommons and low value rares. Sold by weight or by the thousand.
A card sealed in a rigid case by a grading company.
slang.example: A schematic, not a photo of a real slab

slang.meaning: Sending a card away to be authenticated and scored on condition. PSA runs 1 to 10 and is the market standard for Pokemon; BGS and CGC also grade.
A card numbered higher than the set total, like 199/198.
slang.example: Seismitoad, Black Bolt. The corner reads 105/086

slang.meaning: The single letter in the bottom corner. It controls tournament legality and has nothing to do with rarity or value.
slang.example: Metapod, 151. The letter sits after the illustrator credit

gone.name: Pokemon LV.X
gone.note: Played on top of an Active Pokemon. Gold band across the top.

gone.name: Pokemon Prime
gone.note: The word Prime is not printed anywhere on the card. Spot them by the gold name text and spiked artwork edges.

gone.name: Pokemon LEGEND
gone.note: Two card halves that combined into one Pokemon.

gone.name: Pokemon-EX and M Pokemon-EX
gone.note: The uppercase EX. Mega EX ended your turn unless you used a Spirit Link.

gone.name: Pokemon BREAK
gone.note: Printed sideways and stacked on the stage below.

gone.name: Pokemon-GX
gone.note: One GX attack per game. Tag Team GX put two Pokemon on a card and gave up three prizes.

gone.name: Amazing Rare
gone.note: A burst of colour behind the Pokemon that spills out past the frame, and a rainbow letter A in the corner where the star would be. Nine of them exist, six in Vivid Voltage and three in Shining Fates.

sources.for: 'Amazing Pokemon cards are identified by the Amazing Rare card rarity and an illustration with a multi-colored background that goes beyond the frame.' The card list is complete and runs to nine: Celebi, Raikou, Zacian, Zamazenta, Jirachi and Rayquaza in Vivid Voltage, Reshiram, Kyogre and Yveltal in Shining Fates. Nothing after Shining Fates, which is why this is in the retired list.
'Amazing Pokemon were introduced in Vivid Voltage. The background of an Amazing Pokemon is a swirl of multiple colors that extends outside of the box for artwork.'

The corner symbol, checked on all three Shining Fates cards: swsh4.5/17 Reshiram 017/072, swsh4.5/21 Kyogre 021/072 and swsh4.5/46 Yveltal 046/072. Each prints a white capital A on a multicoloured burst, bottom left, in the slot a star would occupy. All three are numbered inside the set total, so they are not secret rares.

gone.name: Rainbow rares
gone.note: Discontinued at Scarlet and Violet. They are not coming out of a modern pack, whatever the glitter on a Special Illustration Rare looks like.

gone.name: Radiant Pokemon
gone.note: Always Basic, one per deck, only worth one prize.
